newsitem.title: CANADA: Syncrude says plant maintenance to end May 8.
newsitem.headline: Syncrude says plant maintenance to end May 8.

text.p: Syncrude Canada Ltd., the world's largest producer of synthetic crude oil, expects a maintenance run that cut output by 100,000 barrels per day to end on May 8, a company spokesman said.

The oil sands mining, bitumen extraction and upgrading operation located north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, began its turnaround on March 29 and was producing at a rate of about 130,000 barrels per day on Tuesday, Syncrude's Peter Marshall said.
Marshall said the operation was expected to pump out 230,000 barrels per day when it resumes full operations.

"The coker went down only last weekend. There's a lot of units being worked on but that's the one most people relate to," Marshall said, adding that about 3,000 people were on site performing various maintenance functions.

Canadian crude oil traders said the Syncrude maintenance run reduced the potential impact of IPL Energy Inc's pipeline outage that began last weekend, halting most of the country's crude oil exports to the United States.
The outage cut exports of about one million barrels of Canadian crude oil per day.

Syncrude's partners include Imperial Oil Ltd, Petro-Canada, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Athabasca Oil Sands Investments Inc, Canadian Oil Sands Investments Inc, Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd unit Mocal Energy Ltd and Murphy Oil Corp.
